name: Easter Purple
lede: Easter Purple is a bright blue-violet from the 2010 xkcd color survey, close kin to lavender and ordinary purple, with no traceable coiner.

sections.title: A crowd name, not a dictionary one
sections.body:
The xkcd color survey asked visitors to type a name next to a random swatch, and "Easter Purple" was the winning label for this one [1]. The survey records only the winning name, not who typed it first or why, so any link to Easter-egg dyeing is a guess, not a documented fact [1]. Two other crowd labels sit almost on the same swatch, Light Purple and Light Urple, each under 2.5 CIEDE2000 units away, which shows how many separate names one patch of hue space can collect [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[bright-lavender]], [[heliotrope]], [[lavender-floral]] and [[floral-lavender]], at 3.3, 5.5, 6.2 and 6.2 ΔE [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the swatch as a brilliant violet, about 10 units off [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds none where this exact violet covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. That fits a pattern across the xkcd survey's most saturated purples: they sit outside what aged pigment and varnish typically produce [3]. A match here would be a computed color comparison, never a claim about pigment [3].
